analysis: The code snippet calls `locals.toArray(new Key[locals.size()])` only when `locals.size() != 0`, ensuring the array is non-null and has a positive size. The list `locals` is an `ArrayList<Key>`, so all its elements are of type `Key`. The array `new Key[locals.size()]` has runtime type `Key[]`, which is a supertype of every element (since `Key` is the exact type). Therefore, neither `ArrayStoreException` (due to type mismatch) nor `NullPointerException` (due to null array) can occur in this context.
remark: Both declared exceptions are fully avoided: `ArrayStoreException` is avoided because the array type `Key[]` is compatible with all list elements; `NullPointerException` is avoided because the array is explicitly created with a non-null value and the guard condition ensures a non-empty list.
